stem: Three Massachusetts-licensed pharmacies are closing on the same date: a non-resident Drug Store pharmacy, a resident sterile compounding pharmacy, and an institutional sterile compounding pharmacy. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Each must give the Board certified written notice at least 14 days before closing.
The non-resident pharmacy must make the post-closure submission of original licences.
The sterile compounding pharmacy must identify a pharmacy able to continue patient care.
The institutional sterile compounding pharmacy is excused from the patient-notice duty.
The continuity-of-care pharmacy identified must be licensed by the Board.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.13 requires certified written notice at least 14 days ahead from resident and non-resident pharmacies alike. 6.13(3) additionally requires a compounding pharmacy to notify the Board of the identity of a pharmacy LICENSED BY THE BOARD that is suitable and available to provide CONTINUITY OF CARE. 6.13(6) expressly does NOT apply to non-resident pharmacies, and 6.13(7) excuses institutional sterile compounding pharmacies from 6.13(3) and 6.13(4).

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the 14-day certified notice is common to both.
choice_analysis.B: The post-closure submission does not apply to non-resident pharmacies.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: 6.13(7) excuses them from the patient-notice duty.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the identified pharmacy must be Board-licensed.

related_facts: A resident pharmacy's post-closure submission is due within 14 days of closure
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates apply one closure checklist uniformly and miss three type-specific variations.
